5
A micrometer is used to measure the diameters of two cylinders.
diameter of first cylinder = (12.78 ± 0.02) mm
diameter of second cylinder = (16.24 ± 0.03) mm
The difference in the diameters is calculated.
What is the uncertainty in this difference?
A
0.01 mm
B
0.02 mm
C
0.03 mm
D
0.05 mm

hints: Notice the question asks for the uncertainty in the difference $16.24 \text{ mm} - 12.78 \text{ mm}$, not the difference itself.
Recall the rule for combining absolute uncertainties when adding or subtracting two measured values with uncertainties $\pm 0.02 \text{ mm}$ and $\pm 0.03 \text{ mm}$.
Add the two absolute uncertainties together and keep the same unit of $\text{mm}$ to get the uncertainty in the calculated difference.
walkthrough: Identify the operation: the difference $d = 16.24 - 12.78$ in $\text{mm}$ is found by subtraction of two independent measurements.
State the rule: when values are added or subtracted, their absolute uncertainties add to give the absolute uncertainty in the result.
Write the uncertainty sum: $\Delta d = \Delta d_1 + \Delta d_2$.
Substitute the given values with units: $\Delta d = 0.02 \text{ mm} + 0.03 \text{ mm} = 0.05 \text{ mm}$.
Check the result: the unit remains $\text{mm}$ and the difference itself would be $3.46 \pm 0.05 \text{ mm}$, so $0.05 \text{ mm}$ is sensible. This is option D.

A.explanation: Subtracting $0.03 - 0.02$ is wrong because absolute uncertainties in a difference add, they do not subtract.

B.explanation: Using only $0.02 \text{ mm}$ ignores the $0.03 \text{ mm}$ uncertainty in the $16.24 \text{ mm}$ diameter.

C.explanation: Using only $0.03 \text{ mm}$ ignores the $0.02 \text{ mm}$ uncertainty in the $12.78 \text{ mm}$ diameter.

D.explanation: For addition or subtraction, add absolute uncertainties: $0.02 + 0.03 = 0.05 \text{ mm}$.
